purpose: Classify current benchmark/evidence families by what public evaluator semantics can soundly eliminate before spending scarce Astra access or fresh private-result access.

route_legend.E_CANDIDATE: Complete load-bearing benchmark evaluator semantics appear explicit/reproducible enough to attempt direct certification, subject to exact target-version byte binding.
route_legend.MIXED_OR_CONDITIONAL: Some scoring semantics are explicit but hidden/private tasks, judge preference, or unreleased criteria remain load-bearing.
route_legend.U_OR_EXTERNAL_RESULT: Public information cannot soundly reconstruct the full load-bearing evaluator/context; use authenticated external result or exact target-law/evaluator access rather than inference.

facts: Terminal-Bench uses executable task validation through an evaluation harness.
Artificial Analysis describes current coding-agent benchmark task outcomes as binary.
findings.boundary: Exact current target version (including TB4 if load-bearing), task set, harness, and evaluator bytes must be frozen. Do not transfer a TB2 proof to TB4.

facts: OSWorld uses execution-based evaluation functions.
OSWorld v2.1 pins code, task, asset, website, and provider-image versions for comparability.
findings.boundary: Some task implementations/assets are gated. Exact evaluator completeness requires the pinned task/evaluator material, not only the public release manifest.

facts: HLE is closed-form and supports automated grading.
Leaderboard evaluation uses a frozen extractor/judge setup, while edge cases such as acceptable precision can depend on judge implementation.
findings.boundary: An E proof is possible only against an exact frozen variant, judge prompt/model, dataset revision, tool policy, and answer-normalization contract. Do not equate HLE-Diamond with a distinct HLE-with-tools target without target binding.

facts: The test split is private.
Each question is graded by weighted checks with dealbreakers.
Per-check judgments are made by a three-model LLM jury.
The primary score is dealbreaker-gated severity-weighted partial credit and models are run three times.
findings.boundary: Public methodology proves score structure but not complete per-context evaluator semantics or private test content. Public reconstruction cannot certify the target score atom.

facts: Public AutomationBench tasks are assertion-based and programmatically verifiable.
Official/private evaluation uses a held-out private task set.
AutomationBench-AA scores objective completion and zeroes a task on guardrail violation.
findings.boundary: Public assertion semantics do not reveal the held-out private task/evaluator instances. Earlier finite-grammar substitution must remain falsified for the private score.

facts: The standard grading protocol is pairwise human expert preference.
Task-specific rubrics improve consistency but human inter-rater agreement is not perfect.
Automated grading is explicitly an approximation rather than a replacement for expert grading.
findings.boundary: Do not collapse expert preference into a deterministic public rubric without proof. Exact published score/result evidence is cheaper and sounder than inferring the hidden preference law.

facts: AA-Briefcase combines binary rubric checks with pairwise analytical-quality and presentation judgments.
Its task set includes private long-horizon professional projects.
findings.boundary: Rubric subscore may admit an E-style route if exact checks are available, but aggregate Elo remains load-bearing on pairwise preference semantics and private tasks.

facts: FrontierCode uses held-out tests plus a maintainer-authored rubric.
Rubric covers correctness, regression safety, build/style cleanliness, and project conventions.
Failing blocker criteria yields zero.
findings.boundary: Public methodology is insufficient to reconstruct held-out tests and full per-task maintainer rubrics. Published result or evaluator access remains irreducible for exact score certification.

facts: The task set contains sealed/private mathematical mechanisms with bounded experiments.
Scoring uses behavior on private probes and a noise-aware normalized-error threshold.
findings.boundary: The public scoring form is not enough to reconstruct private mechanisms/probes. Exact target result or authenticated evaluator execution is irreducible.

facts: The benchmark is public-facing and tool-enabled, but surfaced current rows are largely provider self-reports rather than independent runs.
findings.boundary: Treat self-reported target score as a provenance problem first. Do not spend Astra reasoning budget trying to convert a self-report into independent evidence.
